ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, including terrorist-property provisions; Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 21.1-21.303 and related Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, SOR/2001-512, concerning individuals with significant control. Canada has no general publicly searchable federal UBO register. A federal corporation must maintain an individuals-with-significant-control register and file prescribed information with Corporations Canada; access is generally restricted to the corporation, directors, shareholders in prescribed circumstances, and competent authorities. The 25% test is generally met by ownership or control of 25% or more of voting shares or fair-market-value shares, or by factual control, with control-in-fact and tracing obligations.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Apply risk-based screening before incorporation, banking, payment onboarding, and material ownership changes. Identify domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, heads of international organizations, family members, and close associates under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and FINTRAC guidance. Screen the entity, directors, officers, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signatories, and relevant counterparties against Canadian sanctions administered under the Special Economic Measures Act, Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and United Nations Act; UN Security Council lists; and, where exposure exists, OFAC SDN and related U.S. lists. Document false-positive resolution, ownership and control aggregation, enhanced due diligence, source of wealth and funds, escalation, payment blocking, and suspicious transaction reporting. An ordinary pet-supplies ecommerce corporation is not automatically a PCMLTFA reporting entity, but banks, payment processors, and other reporting entities will independently apply AML/CFT controls.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre, available through Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED): https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/corporations-canada/en
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A federal corporate name must comply with the Canada Business Corporations Act and Canada Business Corporations Regulations, be distinctive and not confusing with existing corporate names, and include a permitted legal element such as Inc., Incorporated, Corp., Corporation, Ltd., or Limited. English, French, or a combination may be used. A French version and an English version may be registered as alternate corporate names if properly filed. Non-Latin characters and transliterations are not automatically prohibited, but the registrability, pronunciation, distinctiveness, and filing-format requirements must be confirmed with Corporations Canada. A NUANS corporate name search report is ordinarily required for a word name unless an exception applies; the report is generally current for 90 days.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Professional titles or regulated designations implying an unauthorized licensed activity
Words that imply sponsorship, affiliation, or endorsement by the Crown, the Government of Canada, a province, or a regulated financial institution
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Canada does not generally provide a separate statutory name-reservation appeal comparable to a formal tribunal appeal. Obtain a current NUANS report, revise the proposed name to address distinctiveness or sensitive-word objections, and resubmit through Corporations Canada. For a disputed rejection, request written reasons or reconsideration from Corporations Canada, provide supporting evidence of consent, non-confusion, or regulatory authorization, and preserve the filing record. If an adverse administrative decision remains material and no adequate internal remedy exists, obtain Canadian administrative-law advice concerning judicial review in the Federal Court under the Federal Courts Act. Provincial registrations require separate provincial registry procedures and may impose different name rules.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A federal corporation must maintain a registered office in the province specified in its articles under the Canada Business Corporations Act and must maintain prescribed corporate records. A commercial virtual office may be acceptable if it is a real, serviceable physical address, can receive legal process and official correspondence, and supports access to corporate records. A post-office box alone is generally insufficient. For pet-supplies ecommerce, a virtual registered office is generally permissible at incorporation, but it does not substitute for operational evidence such as inventory, fulfillment arrangements, payment-processing records, tax records, customer-support capability, and adequate books and records. Provincial extra-provincial registrations may impose additional local-office requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No routine unannounced incorporation inspection is generally required for a low-risk pet-supplies ecommerce company. Estimated annual likelihood of an unannounced physical verification visit is below 5% absent a complaint, sanctions concern, tax anomaly, suspected fraud, licensing issue, or AML red flag. This is an operational risk estimate, not a statutory probability. CRA, FINTRAC, provincial authorities, payment processors, landlords, and banks may conduct verification or request evidence without relying on a formal incorporation inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required; no escrow account mandated. Directors may authorize share issuance for any fair consideration as permitted by the CBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada, ISED - Canadian Corporate Name Search via a NUANS accredited provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search request through a NUANS accredited provider or via Corporations Canada. Verify that the proposed name is not confusingly similar to existing federal or provincial entities. Reserve the name for a period of 90 days if required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusing, submit a written argument demonstrating distinctiveness, or select a new name and re-file the search.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada (online portal or paper filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 4001, including the corporate name, authorized share structure, restrictions on business (if any), number or name of first directors, and registered office address. Ensure the articles are signed by each incorporator and any consents are attached.
required_dossiers: List of first directors (Form 4002 or in articles)
Consent to act as director (for each director, if not included in Form 4001)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Corporations Canada issues a deficiency notice, correct the stated defect in the articles and resubmit within the specified response window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles and Obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the articles electronically through the Corporations Canada online filing service or by mail. Pay the applicable filing fee (CAD $200 equivalent). Upon approval, the Director issues a Certificate of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected for omissions, amend and resubmit; fees are generally retained and applied to the corrected filing unless otherwise advised.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene First Board Meeting and Adopt Organization Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of directors or obtain unanimous written consent to: adopt the pro-forma board resolution approving share subscriptions, appoint officers, adopt Bylaw No. 1, and fix the registered office. Record all decisions in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Notice of first board meeting or consent to resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum is not achievable, postpone the meeting and obtain a written resolution signed by all directors in lieu of a meeting, as permitted under the CBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for CRA Business Number and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a federal Business Number (BN) through CRA’s online portal, by telephone, or by mail. Register for corporate income tax, GST/HST where applicable, and payroll deductions if employees are anticipated. Provide the Certificate of Incorporation to verify corporate identity.
required_dossiers: Director identification (name, address, SIN if resident)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the application, respond with supporting corporate documents and confirm the entity’s registration details to clear the hold.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for e-commerce retail; municipal zoning and business licensing may apply in the operating municipality
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No federal industrial operating permit required under ISIC 4791 (Pet Supplies E-commerce)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) – only applicable if a physical installation triggers federal assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no federal EIA required for pure e-commerce retail
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for e-commerce sales; any warehouse operation must comply with provincial and municipal wastewater, VOC, and waste handling codes

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No special federal fire or structural permit is required. If a fulfillment warehouse is operated, obtain local fire safety certification, structural load inspection, and workplace safety clearance from the provincial authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes/child-and-family-benefits.html? Actually official portal is https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity must apply for a Business Number (BN) and a GST/HST account through the CRA's registration process for non-residents. The CRA accepts Form RC1, a written application containing the legal name, jurisdiction of incorporation, directors/officers, Canadian agent contact details, and declaration of the nature of taxable supplies. The CRA validates the information and issues a nine-digit BN followed by an RP (regular partner) or RT (GST/HST) program account reference. For GST/HST registration, the applicant must certify that it is engaged in commercial activity in Canada and either exceeds the CAD 30,000 registration threshold or wishes to voluntarily register. Applications may be submitted by mail, fax, or electronically through an authorized tax representative using the CRA's Represent a Client portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election. A federally incorporated business corporation is a separate taxpayer under the Income Tax Act and a distinct registrant under the Excise Tax Act. Specific elections relevant to tax grouping include the Excise Tax Act section 156 election (GST/HST group registration) and the section 156(3) election for closely related corporations to treat inter-corporate supplies as not taxable. For income tax purposes, hybrid mismatch arrangement elections and the associated corporations election under Income Tax Act section 256(2) may apply; however, these do not alter the fundamental corporation-level taxation of active business income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or cumulative across the last four consecutive calendar quarters; non-residents carrying on business in Canada and making taxable supplies may be required to register earlier if they invoice or advertise in Canada and meet the threshold test.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no federal real-time fiscal clearance, electronic invoicing approval, or digital stamping mandate for GST/HST purposes. Registrants whose annual worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 1 million must file GST/HST returns electronically using the GST/HST NETFILE system or through a third-party service provider. Electronic invoices must contain prescribed tax information and records must be retained for six years. The CRA may require specified supporting data files during an audit but does not impose an API-based clearance gateway.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Tangible personal property is zero-rated under paragraph 21(a) of the Excise Tax Act where the supplier exports the goods, or ships the goods to a non-resident for export, as soon after the supply is made as is reasonably possible. The zero-rating also extends to goods supplied to a non-resident where the goods are exported as a direct accompaniment of the non-resident. For services, zero-rating may be claimed when the service is supplied to a non-resident and is not in respect of real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time; services rendered in relation to exported goods may also qualify under section 22. For an e-commerce pet supplies business, the sale of physical goods to customers located in the United States or other foreign jurisdictions, with the goods shipped out of Canada under documentary proof of export, will qualify for 0% GST/HST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canadian export documentation as transmitted via the Canadian Export Reporting System, GCAAS/CES)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical movement out of Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank payment evidence showing foreign-source settlement in a non-Canadian currency
Commercial invoice with explicit zero-rating indicator and cross-reference to the proof of export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA periodically audits exporters and may deny zero-rating where the documentation bundle is incomplete or the goods were not actually exported within a reasonable time. Where a zero-rating claim is found to be false or fraudulent, the taxpayer is reassessed for the full GST/HST amount not collected, plus statutory interest from the due date. The Excise Tax Act imposes a penalty of 50% of the net tax amount where a person knowingly, or under circumstances of gross negligence, makes a false statement in a return or application; wilful evasion may result in criminal prosecution. Additionally, failure to collect or remit GST/HST can render directors and corporate officers personally liable for the unremitted amounts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a free current account convertibility regime compliant with IMF Article VIII. Capital account transactions are generally convertible with limited restrictions applicable to non-residents, such as real estate acquisitions. Profit remittances to foreign shareholders are permitted without prior approval for most corporate entities, subject to Canada Revenue Agency reporting and applicable withholding taxes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the Bank of Canada is required. Exporters may convert foreign exchange receipts at prevailing market rates. All foreign exchange transactions must be reported through authorized dealers to the Bank of Canada. For e-commerce retail operations, direct conversion via payment processors such as Stripe or PayPal constitutes standard compliant practice.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility rating for Stripe and PayPal given their Canadian licensing under the Payment Services Regulation Act and integration with domestic clearing rails. Legal constraints include mandatory FINTRAC anti-money laundering compliance, PCI DSS data security standards, and adherence to the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person physical appearance of directors and authorized signers is mandatory for corporate account opening and KYC interviews. Remote video KYC is permitted solely for existing clients or in limited low-risk scenarios as determined by the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate ownership chart, shareholder agreements, board resolutions, and percentage-based control documentation

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and wealth verification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements, audited financial statements, tax returns, and independent third-party verification letters

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and politically exposed persons screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP declarations, adverse media reports, and certified clean screening results

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections routed via SWIFT MT103 wires or correspondent banking with purpose code 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection'. Verification requires board resolutions, shareholder agreements, and source-of-funds documentation. All transactions must comply with the Exchange Control Act and be reported to the Bank of Canada.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements cleared through SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers or Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 for trade settlements. E-commerce pet supplies payments processed via Stripe or PayPal rails with final settlement to Canadian bank accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Director appointed under the Canada Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Summary conviction offence under s. 123 CBCA with a maximum fine of CAD 5,000; continued non-filing for one year or more triggers a Director's default notice and administrative dissolution under s. 212 CBCA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Federal Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end due June 30); balance of tax payable is due 3 months after year-end for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (2 months for other corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months under s. 162(1) Income Tax Act; repeat failure penalty increases to 10%; prescribed interest accrues on unpaid tax and penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (federal goods and services tax on e-commerce retail sales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end for annual filers; the annual filing election is available only if total business revenue does not exceed CAD 1.5 million; monthly and quarterly filers must file by the applicable Business Window of 1 month or 3 months after each reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the net unremitted amount (10% for repeat non-compliance) under s. 280 Excise Tax Act plus daily interest at prescribed rates under s. 280.1; persistent default cancels the annual filing election and may trigger mandatory electronic filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO) Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (filed through the federal Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed simultaneously with the Annual Return within 60 days after the incorporation anniversary; any change in significant control, including a share transfer creating 25% or more ownership or de facto control, must be recorded in the ISC register within 15 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Knowingly providing false or misleading ISC information is punishable by a fine up to CAD 200,000 and/or imprisonment up to 6 months; directors and officers who fail to maintain an accurate register are liable to summary conviction fines up to CAD 5,000; the register must be produced to Corporations Canada and CRA upon demand.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The CBCA requires an independent auditor for every corporation by default; the audit may be waived only for a non-distributing private corporation through a unanimous resolution of all shareholders for each fiscal year; distributing (public) corporations and federally regulated banks, trust, insurance and loan companies cannot dispense with the audit. No revenue or asset size exemption exists under the CBCA.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) applies to publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Part II) is the governing local GAAP for this private e-commerce retail corporation; income tax is computed under s. 9 Income Tax Act by adjusting accounting net income for CRA-required differences.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every CBCA corporation must prepare and maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control and update it within 15 days of any share transfer creating 25% or more direct or indirect ownership, voting rights, or de facto control; annual confirmation of the register's accuracy and completeness is filed through the federal Annual Return; the register must be disclosed to CRA and Corporations Canada upon lawful demand; false statements expose the responsible individual to fines up to CAD 200,000 and/or 6 months' imprisonment.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Shareholders) with share transfer ledger
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC / UBO)
Minute Book (board and shareholder resolutions, by-laws, and meeting records)
Securities Register (all issued share classes and transfer history)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 220 - 450 per year (CAD 300 - 600), covering registered office and records address, corporate agent services, and Annual Return preparation
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if the audit is waived by unanimous shareholder resolution; otherwise USD 15,000 - 35,000 (CAD 20,000 - 47,000) for a full ASPE audit of the retail e-commerce entity, or USD 4,000 - 11,000 (CAD 6,000 - 15,000) for a review engagement if approved by shareholders

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% (federal general corporate rate; 9% federal rate on the first CAD 500,000 of Canadian active business income for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) under the Small Business Deduction)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (19 percentage-point reduction for a CCPC on active business income up to the CAD 500,000 business limit); General Rate Reduction (13 percentage points, embedded in the 15% headline rate); SR&ED investment tax credits (40% refundable for qualifying CCPCs, 15% non-refundable for others); accelerated capital cost allowance for qualifying computing equipment; Federal-provincial tax collection agreements mean provincial corporate tax (e.g., Ontario 10%, Alberta 8%) is imposed separately but coordinated through the T2 system.
